description:
Tests that run a child process (elixir for an oracle, fz2, a built binary) give it a 20 second wall-clock limit. Under machine load the child is starved and the limit fires although the program is correct, so a full gate fails for a reason unrelated to the change under test. A wall-clock limit on a child measures the machine, not the program.

Evidence, all three pass when run alone:
- oracle_goldens_match_elixir: elixir runs of fixtures2/behavior/binary_over_threshold and callable_union_capture_containment exceeded 20 s in a full gate at load average 57-100 (fz-rs7.4 builder gate). Alone the test passed (1167 s total).
- matrix::00562_mailbox_closure_each::build: 'built binary exceeded 20s' once at high load; passed alone.
- json_roundtrip::run: a 20 s readiness timeout in a full gate at load average above 60 (fz-348.2 builder gate); passed alone (3 of 3).

One concept, either form: the limit is on the child's own CPU time (so a starved child is not charged for waiting), or child runs are serialized so load cannot starve them. Raising the 20 s number is not the fix; it moves the flake.

The limit lives in tests/fixture_matrix.rs (DEFAULT_FIXTURE_HANG_TIMEOUT, 20 s) and exists to catch a hang. A hung child uses no CPU, so a pure CPU-time limit would not catch it; the design has to keep hang detection (for example a much longer wall-clock ceiling beside the CPU limit, or serialized runs with the existing limit). Decide between the two forms with a spike under load before building.

Fails before, passes after: a test of the limit helper in which a child starved of CPU for longer than the limit is not reported as exceeding, a child that burns CPU past the limit is, and a child that hangs is.

Acceptance: full gate green; a full gate run alongside two other full gates on the same machine shows no limit failure.
title: A test's limit on a child process measures the child, not the machine
